ev.q: Mean weekly ED visit counts, surveillance period
By fall 2022, mean weekly adolescent ED visits were decreasing for MHCs overall (−11%), suicide-related behaviors (−12%), and drug overdoses (−10%) compared with fall 2021

changes.why: Period-to-period changes reported separately by sex are a series over time by group, which the brief counts as comparison, not stratification; there is no adjustment, standardization or model.

value.name: CI vs fixed value
value.inferred_from: VR 95% CIs read against 1 ('lower' VR 0.94 vs 'similar' VR 0.97 among males); CI method not named

ev.q: Visit ratios (VRs)** with 95% CIs were calculated to describe the proportion of ED visits of interest among all adolescent ED visits
among males, the proportion of suicide-related behaviors was lower (VR = 0.94) and for drug overdose (VR = 0.97) was similar

changes.why: The headline claims (decreased/stable/increased) rest on percent-change thresholds, which are arithmetic plus quantization; VR CIs support only the secondary proportion statements.

value.referent: corresponding school-semester period in 2021 (recent change) and 2019 (prepandemic baseline)

ev.q: were compared with corresponding periods in 2021 and 2019 to monitor recent changes in ED visits and differences from the prepandemic baseline, respectively
Absolute change in mean weekly ED visit counts ¶¶ (%)

changes.why: The referent is two comparison periods, not fall 2021 alone; framework and scale are unchanged.

ev.q: CDC examined changes in U.S. emergency department (ED) visits for mental health conditions (MHCs) overall
drug-involved overdoses (including opioids) among children and adolescents aged 12–17 years (adolescents)
The drug overdose classification identifies acute drug poisonings from any type of drug
identifies ED visits related to suicidal ideation, self-harm, and suspected suicide attempts

changes.why: Drug overdoses are defined as acute poisonings and suicide-related behaviors include self-harm, both outcomes in their own right.

equity.level_reason: Age defines the population and sex is a stratifier; sex differences ("particularly among adolescent females") are described without social-position or disparity framing, so age/sex alone gives level 0.

level_alternative.reason: Sex-specific results are reported and the text emphasizes the burden among females, which a looser reading of social-position framing could treat as group-specific results by an SPD.

ev.q: among children and adolescents aged 12–17 years (adolescents)
Differences by sex were observed; levels among females were at or higher than prepandemic baselines for these conditions.

determinants_of_health.v: return to prepandemic-like school and community environments; social engagement and isolation; adverse childhood experiences; accessible behavioral health care (988 crisis line, telehealth)

ev.q: Many adolescents have returned to prepandemic-like school and community environments, which might have improved social engagement, reduced isolation
Familial or other stressors might also have declined, resulting in fewer adverse childhood experiences
federal investments, such as the 988 suicide crisis line***** and improvements to accessible behavioral health care (e.g., telehealth)

notes: Determinants are offered as possible explanations of the overall trend, not of a disparity. Percent-change thresholds (±10%) classify changes and are not tests.
